summary: Defines MIB objects for managing SMDS access interfaces with SNMP network management, using the SMIv2 format. SMDS is a high-speed data service offered by carriers. This is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: A list of dials and gauges that a network manager can read to see how a special data service connection is doing.

questions: how to manage smds interfaces with snmp
which smds interface objects moved to iftable
subtitle: SNMP objects for watching SMDS access links, rewritten for SNMPv2 and folded into the standard interfaces table.

tldr.problem: Operators needed a standard way to monitor SMDS access interfaces over SNMP, and the earlier definition in RFC 1304 predated the improved interpretation of the MIB-II interfaces group.
tldr.mechanism: The memo defines the SIP-MIB module in SNMPv2 format. Counters that an interface already has move into the standard ifTable, and the module keeps only SMDS-specific groups for Level 3, Level 2, PLCP, IP over SMDS, an error log and DXI.
tldr.outcome: It replaces RFC 1304 with a module that is semantically identical to it, while deprecating the objects that ifTable now carries.

today: RFC 1694 is a Draft Standard that obsoletes RFC 1304. The Draft Standard status and the obsoleted RFC come from the RFC's own metadata; the text itself records no later developments.

sections.title: What the Memo Defines
sections.content:
RFC 1694 defines part of the Management Information Base (MIB) for managing SMDS access interfaces. It covers four access protocols: SIP, SIP/DXI, SIP/FR and SIP/ATM.

The memo replaces RFC 1304. It writes the module in the SNMPv2 SMI and says it is semantically identical to the existing RFC 1304 definitions. It also assumes the MIB-II Interfaces group as described in RFC 1573.

It does not cover subscription or configuration of Subscriber-Network Interfaces (SNIs). Those objects live in a separate SMDS Subscription MIB.
sections.eli5: It is a rulebook for the dials on a special data line. It swaps out an older rulebook but keeps the dials meaning the same things.

sections.title: The SNMPv2 Framework Behind It
sections.content:
The memo builds on the SNMPv2 Network Management Framework. That framework has four parts: RFC 1442 for the SMI that names and describes objects, RFC 1213 for MIB-II, RFC 1445 for administrative aspects, and RFC 1448 for the protocol used to reach managed objects. It also uses RFC 1443 for textual conventions and RFC 1444 for conformance statements.

Managed objects are reached through a virtual information store, the MIB. Each object has a name (an object identifier), a syntax written in a restricted subset of ASN.1, and an encoding that follows the ASN.1 basic encoding rules.
sections.eli5: All the gauges follow the same labeling rules, so any manager's tool can find and read them.

sections.title: SMDS Access Stacks and What This MIB Covers
sections.content:
SMDS can be reached through several interface protocols. A SIP-based access runs SIP Level 3, SIP Level 2, a PLCP layer and SIP Level 1. DXI-based access runs SIP Level 3 over DXI Level 2 and DXI Level 1. ATM-based and Frame Relay-based access run SIP Level 3 directly over ATM or Frame Relay.

This memo defines objects only for the layers marked in its figures: SIP Level 3, SIP Level 2, the SIP PLCP and DXI Level 2. The lower layers are managed by other MIB modules, which the memo cites by reference (for example the DS1/E1 and DS3/E3 modules, RFC 1406 and RFC 1407, and the ATM and Frame Relay modules, RFC 1695 and RFC 1604).
sections.eli5: A data line is built like a stack of layers. This rulebook only covers some layers, and other rulebooks cover the rest.

sections.title: Moving Counters into ifTable
sections.content:
With the improved reading of the MIB-II interfaces group, many SIP Level 3 counters can live in the standard ifTable. The objects from RFC 1304 that this covers are deprecated here, and the ifTable objects are to be used instead. No semantics changed; only the object identifiers and descriptors did. For example, sipL3ReceivedIndividualDAs becomes ifInUcastPkts and sipL3Errors becomes ifInErrors.

The memo fixes how SMDS fills the table: ifType is 31, ifMtu is 9232, and ifPhysAddress is an 8-byte value holding the 16-digit Binary Coded Decimal SMDS address. For SIP-based SNIs, ifInOctets is the sipL2ReceivedCounts value multiplied by 44. The discard and output error counters are always zero, and the broadcast counters are not applicable and always zero.

Implementation experience showed that sipL3UnrecognizedIndividualDAs and sipL3UnrecognizedGAs were not supported. Both are marked deprecated.
sections.eli5: Some gauges already exist on every network port, so this memo points to those instead of making new ones.

sections.title: Level 2 Counters and the Level 3 Error Log
sections.content:
The SIP Level 2 table counts Level 2 PDUs received and sent, plus specific error kinds: header check sequence or payload CRC errors, payload length errors, sequence number errors, and message identifier (MID) errors. A payload length error is, for example, a BOM or COM payload not equal to 44 octets.

The SIP Level 3 error log is a table indexed by interface and error type. Each entry keeps the latest source address, destination address and a timestamp. There are 12 error types, such as an invalid BAsize value, a Beginning-End tag mismatch, and an MRI timeout. When the timestamp is zero, the entry holds no valid information. All these errors are counted in sipL3Errors.
sections.eli5: When a message arrives broken, a counter goes up, and a logbook remembers the latest mistake of each kind and when it happened.

sections.title: PLCP, IP over SMDS and DXI Groups
sections.content:
The DS1 and DS3 PLCP groups each report Severely Errored Framing Seconds, an alarm state (noAlarm, receivedFarEndAlarm or incomingLOF) and Unavailable Seconds.

The IP over SMDS table supports RFC 1209. For each IP address on an interface it gives the SMDS individual address of the station, the group address of the Logical IP Subnetwork, and the address ARP requests go to. The memo notes that agents may make these read-only objects writable at their discretion.

The DXI table reports the frame checksum type (CRC16 or CRC32), discarded and errored frames, aborts, test frames and Heart Beat Poll no-acknowledgement timeouts. A carrier selection group is defined only as a placeholder.
sections.eli5: Other groups watch the physical line for trouble, record which addresses an IP network uses, and count problems on a simpler kind of connection.

sections.title: Conformance and Security
sections.content:
The compliance statement makes the SIP Level 3 group mandatory for every SMDS interface. The other groups are mandatory only where they apply: Level 2 for interfaces that run SIP Level 2, the DS1 or DS3 PLCP groups for interfaces that run those PLCPs, the IP group for interfaces running IP over SMDS per RFC 1209, and the DXI group for DXI-SNI interfaces.

The Security Considerations section says only that security issues are not discussed in this memo.
sections.eli5: Every device must have the basic gauges. The special gauges are only needed if the device uses that feature.

items.label: invalidBAsizeFieldValue
items.desc: BAsize value out of range or not a multiple of 4 octets.

items.label: invalidHdrExtLength
items.desc: Header Extension Length not equal to 3.

items.label: invalidHdrExtElementLength
items.desc: Header Extension element length greater than 12.

items.label: invalidHdrExtCarSelectElementPositionLenghtValueOrFormat
items.desc: Carrier Selection element misplaced or wrong.

items.label: beTagMismatch
items.desc: Beginning-End tags in header and trailer differ.

items.label: baSizeFieldNotEqualToLengthField
items.desc: BAsize does not equal the Length field.

items.label: incorrectLength
items.desc: Length field does not match the PDU.

items.label: mriTimeout
items.desc: Time between BOM and EOM exceeded the MRI.
